Compute Krippendorff's alpha across raters

Source: R/api-krippendorff-alpha.R
krippendorff_alpha_table.Rd

Estimate observed-score agreement across two or more raters, allowing unequal numbers of ratings per unit. This is Krippendorff's agreement coefficient, not Cronbach's internal-consistency alpha or MFRM separation reliability. No measurement-model fitting is performed.

Usage

krippendorff_alpha_table(
  data,
  rater,
  unit,
  score,
  level = c("nominal", "ordinal", "interval", "ratio"),
  categories = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Long-format data with at most one row per rater and unit.

rater

Name of the rater identifier column.

unit

Names of columns jointly identifying a rated unit, for example c("Person", "Task"). They match observations, not variance components.

score

Name of the score column. Missing scores are NA. Nominal/ordinal scores may be numeric, character, factor or logical; factors compare by labels. Interval/ratio scores must be finite numeric values, and ratio scores must be nonnegative with a meaningful zero.

level

Measurement level: "nominal" (default), "ordinal", "interval" or "ratio". Choose on substantive grounds; numeric category codes alone do not establish an interval or ratio scale.

categories

For ordinal scores, the required distinct category values in their substantive order. Factor levels and numeric spacing never silently set this order. For nominal scores, optional permitted values; if NULL, observed nonmissing values are used. Values must have the same numeric/character/logical representation as score (factors use labels). Unused categories are allowed. Leave NULL for interval/ratio scores.

Value

A plain list with table (alpha, observed/expected disagreement, availability and sample counts), counts (category values, nonmissing and pairable counts, plus ordinal positions), cases (input rows and exclusion reasons), unit_summary (assignment counts and unit disagreements), units (unique input unit keys), settings and notes. Unit indexes rows of units. Save with base::saveRDS(); export data frames with utils::write.csv(). Reopening the saved list performs no calculation.

Details

The coefficient is \(1-D_o/D_e\). Only units with at least two nonmissing scores contribute to either disagreement. A unit with m ratings contributes its ordered rating pairs divided by m-1 to the coincidence counts, hence contributes m pairable ratings overall. Units are not equally weighted when m differs. The expected disagreement draws two distinct observations without replacement from the pooled pairable ratings, with denominator n(n-1), where n is the number of pairable ratings. This is not Cohen's kappa chance model or MFRM model-implied expected agreement.

The squared difference function is 0/1 mismatch for nominal scores, frequency-based rank distance for ordinal scores, squared numeric difference for interval scores, and \(((c-k)/(c+k))^2\) for ratio scores (0 when both values are zero). Ordinal positions use cumulative pairable-category counts minus half the category count, divided by n. The squared difference between these positions is proportional to Krippendorff's ordinal distance. It is not quadratic weighting of category numbers or equally spaced category ranks. Unused ranks and singleton-only categories do not alter pairable distances.

Interval distances are calculated after subtracting score_offset, dividing by score_half_range, and dividing by 2, using only pairable values to set the offset and half-range. Constant pairable values map to zero. This avoids squaring very large or tiny raw scores. The common normalization leaves alpha unchanged; reported disagreements are on this normalized scale, not original squared score units. Ordinal positions are similarly normalized by n. Nominal and ratio disagreements use their stated distance directly. Computation avoids a dense category-by-category matrix. Ratio computation still requires quadratic time in the number of distinct pairable values.

No rows are imputed and repeated rater-unit cells are rejected, including repetitions with missing scores. All input rows remain in cases. unit_summary distinguishes missing scores on assigned rows from absent assignments relative to the observed rater roster. Units with no input rows at all are unknown to the function. Missingness and selective assignment may affect representativeness; numerical handling does not correct that bias.

Negative estimates are retained. With no pairable ratings or zero expected disagreement, alpha is unavailable with a reason rather than set to 0 or 1. A finite coefficient describes this pooled rating sample, not each rater's accuracy against a reference or a guarantee of interchangeable ratings. There are no confidence intervals, tests, quality cutoffs or bootstrap claims. Dependencies among several tasks from one person require attention in any subsequent sampling inference. Circular, bipolar and custom metrics are not implemented.

References

Krippendorff, K. (2011; literature updated 2013). Computing Krippendorff's Alpha-Reliability. Sections A-E, pp. 1-10. https://www.asc.upenn.edu/krippendorffs-alpha-reliability

See also

pairwise_icc_table(), interrater_agreement_table(), score_comparison_table()

Examples

data("mfrmr_example_agreement", package = "mfrmr")
ratings <- mfrmr_example_agreement
agreement <- krippendorff_alpha_table(ratings, rater = "Rater",
  unit = c("Person", "Task"), score = "Score", level = "ordinal", categories = 0:3)
agreement$table
#>       Alpha   Level    Status ObservedDisagreement ExpectedDisagreement Raters

#>   Units PairableUnits PairableRatings NonmissingRatings MissingScores
#> 1    12            12              34                34             1
#>   SingletonUnits UnratedUnits
#> 1              0            0
